messages.subject: Re: trouble in read in 4 way cross data
parts:
Could you email the file to me, and allow me to assist you to get the
data into R?

While R/qtl has facilities for analyzing a certain kind of phase-known
4-way cross, the read.cross() function is not actually set up to read
such data into R. I'm not aware of anyone (other than me) using the
4-way cross aspects of the software, and so I've not worked on making
those aspects accessible.

karl
kbr...@jhsph.edu

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: trouble in read in 4 way cross data
parts:
Here again, I responded directly to the author, but thought I should
also respond to the group, on the off chance that someone else is
interested.

I slightly modified the function read.cross.csv() so that it will work
with 4-way cross data. Email me to get the revised code, or wait until
the next release of the software.

To read in 4-way cross data, you need to do something like the
following:

x <- read.cross("csv", "", "4waycross.csv", genotypes=NULL)

"genotypes=NULL" tells the function to not modify the genotype codes,
which must be set up within the file.

karl
